info.title: keywork
info.description: The keywork workspace server: the in-process event bus over HTTP and SSE. Bound to 127.0.0.1 with a per-launch bearer token.

get.summary: This OpenAPI 3.1 document. `info.version` is the keywork release; `info.x-keywork-contract` (also the `x-keywork-contract` response header) is the HTTP and SSE contract version a client checks before it trusts the rest.

Server-sent events: every bus envelope as `event: <type>` plus `data: <envelope json>`. Send `Last-Event-ID` to resume from a retained id (0 replays everything still retained); without it the stream starts live. `?session=<id>` keeps that session's envelopes plus every process-level envelope (an empty `sessionId`), on replay and live alike. Every 15 seconds the server writes a `: keepalive` comment, so a client that hears nothing for longer knows the server is gone rather than quiet.

Session summaries, newest first, each carrying what a desk needs to say working, needs-you or back for a session no client has opened, from what this server already holds: `live` is true when the session is open in this server process (its agent loaded), as on `GET /sessions/{id}`; `working` is true while a turn runs, settles or has a prompt waiting in its queue here; `waiting` counts the asks pending on the session (`asks`) and names the tools they are for (`tools`); `changes`, present once a mutating call of the session has been announced on `changes.updated`, sums that listing as `{ files, added, deleted }` against the session-start baseline.

post.summary: Create an empty session in this workspace.

get.summary: One session with its messages. `asOf` is the latest /events id the messages already reflect, so a client that opened the stream first can drop buffered envelopes with `id <= asOf`. `summaries` marks the messages that are not prompts but folded history, each `{ index, entryId, kind }` with `index` into `messages` and `kind` either `compaction` or `branch_summary`, so a client draws a summary as a summary rather than as something the person typed. `flushes` marks the memory flushes the same way, each `{ index, entryId, facts }`: `messages[index]` is the prompt keywork sent to ask what was worth keeping (not a turn, never counted among the prompts `POST /sessions/{id}/restore` numbers), `messages[index + 1]` the model's reply, and `facts` the lines the reply kept, empty when nothing was worth keeping. `edits` says where the context edits of `POST /sessions/{id}/forget` sit, each `{ index, entryId, role, kind, text }`: `entryId` and `role` name the edited message, `kind` is `forgotten` (the message left `messages`, and `index` is where it sat, before the message that now follows it) or `rewritten` (it is `messages[index]`, carrying its replacement), and `text` is its own text before the edit (empty for a tool result). `reports` lists the one-line summaries a creature's finished threads sent to this conversation (`keywork.creature.report` entries: never prompts, never in the model context), each `{ index, entryId, at, text, origin, kind? }` with `index` the position in `messages` the entry was written before and `origin` the `{ kind: creature, creature, thread }` the live `extension.notice` carried, so a transcript draws the line after a reload exactly as it drew it live (since contract 1.10); `kind: frame` says `messages[index]` is the prompt an inject with `frame` wrote right after it, which a transcript draws as the creature line and never as a keeper prompt (since contract 1.11). `live` is true when the session is open in this server process.

delete.summary: Move a session to the trash: its log and spilled tool output leave the session directory together, so `GET /sessions` stops listing it at once, and `POST /trash/{id}/restore` brings it back whole. An open idle session is closed first; a session with a running turn is refused. Memory notes the session wrote stay (they carry its id as `origin_session`), and forks keep pointing at it: `GET /sessions/{fork}` then reports `forkedFrom.removed`. Fires `session.removed`.

409.description: A turn is running.

post.summary: Append a user prompt and run a turn. `behavior` defaults to `queue`: when a turn is already running the prompt waits behind it, which is what Enter does in the terminal composer. `steer` interrupts the running turn and runs this prompt before anything queued. `now` is the terminal's ctrl+enter: every prompt waiting in the queue is set aside (dropped from the queue and handed back in `setAside`, so a client can offer them again) and this one steers. When the policy would ask, a `gate.ask` event names the call and the turn waits on POST /asks/{callId}; an unanswered ask times out as a headless denial. Progress arrives on /events and a `session.state` envelope follows acceptance.

202.description: The prompt was accepted; `queued` says whether it waits behind a running turn, and with `behavior: "now"`, `setAside` lists the prompts taken off the queue as `queue.changed` carried them. Watch /events for the turn.

400.description: The body is not `{ text, behavior?: "steer" | "queue" | "now" }`.

post.summary: Submit a prompt from a client outside keywork, such as a voice assistant or another LLM window. It runs exactly like a typed prompt: it starts a turn when the session is idle and joins the back of the queue when a turn is running. `turn.started` and `queue.changed` carry `origin: { kind: "external", client }`, the turn answers to the same permission policy and ask queue, and any memory note it proposes is staged with provenance `untrusted`. With `frame: { creature }` the text is a frame the creature answers, never a keeper prompt (since contract 1.11): the origin is `{ kind: "creature", creature, thread }` with `thread` this session, a `keywork.creature.report` entry with `kind: frame` is written before the prompt so `GET /sessions/{id}` marks it under `reports` with the prompt at `messages[index]`, the live `extension.notice` carries `detail.kind: frame`, and the session takes the creature name as its title until the first reply of the creature titles it.

202.description: The prompt was accepted; `queued` is true when it waits behind a running turn.

400.description: The body is not `{ text, client, frame?: { creature } }`.

post.summary: Interrupt the session's running turn, if any.

get.summary: Tool calls waiting on a person: every unanswered `gate.ask`, oldest first. Each carries `rules`, what a `session` or `workspace` answer would record, and for a `write` or `edit` the same `preview` its `gate.ask` carried: `{ path, before, after }`, the file as it is and as the call would leave it.

post.summary: Answer a pending ask. The turn resumes with the verdict and reports it as `gate.permission` with `gate: "user"` and the `scope` of a grant. `scope` defaults to `once`; `session` records the ask's `rules` for the rest of this session and `workspace` records them for every session of this workspace (see `GET /permissions`). A denial ignores `scope` and may say why with `reason`: `unsafe` (the call should not run), `not-now` (the moment, not the call) or `other`, and in the person's own words with `note` (at most 1000 characters, the free text an `other` answer asks for). Both reach the model in the refused call's result, with a line telling it not to retry the call and not to report it as done, and ride on the `gate.permission` decision and in the journal. A grant ignores `reason` and `note`. Only `bash` and MCP calls can be granted beyond `once`. A grant beyond `once` fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ verdict: "granted" | "denied", scope?: "once" | "session" | "workspace", reason?: "unsafe" | "not-now" | "other", note?: string }`, or the call cannot be granted beyond `once` (`write` and `edit` never can, nor a command with no part to remember).

404.description: No ask with that callId is pending.

409.description: That ask was already answered or timed out.

get.summary: The whole memory vault at a glance: the layers notes live in (`workspace`, one `arc:<slug>` per active arc), the review inbox as raw staged items, this process's mutation ledger, the vault's curation audit, the gardener's last sweep and every arc waiting at the airlock. `trusted: false` means the workspace is untrusted and memory is inert: every list is empty and every write answers 403.

200.description: The overview, or the inert shape when the workspace is untrusted.

get.summary: Items waiting for a person: untrusted writes held in staging and the gardener's review proposals, each as the engine's `StagedItem` with its `kind`. The admission policy never lands what an untrusted source wrote (a web page, a workshop's output, another creature's message): it waits here, and its staged write names the source in `source` (`web:<origin>`, `workshop:<id>`, `creature:<slug>`) and whom it was for in `for` (`creature:<slug>` when it reached that creature, else `keeper`; an item staged before addressees reads `keeper`), so approve admits it and discard drops it. `count` is the number the `memory.inbox` event carries.

200.description: The staged items and their count.

post.summary: Land a staged item: a staged write moves to its target note, daily log or map; a proposal is applied. Fires `memory.inbox` with the new count. The answer is the engine's `WriteResult` (`path`, `staged`, `ledgerId`) when the workspace store landed it, or `{}` when a bot's own store did.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No staged item has that id.

post.summary: Drop a staged item without landing it. Fires `memory.inbox` with the new count.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No staged item has that id.

get.summary: Every note the agent can recall, as the engine's `Note` plus the layer it lives in, its file on disk, whether the bootstrap injects it into the system prompt, how often it was recalled since the last sweep and its curing stage (0 raw, 1 has a confidence, 2 has proved useful, 3 settled). A creature's craft memory, what it learned about its own work as distinct from the keeper's notes, is the named section of its layer whose notes carry `section: craft` in their frontmatter; where a note came from rides in `origin_source` (and `origin_creature`). `?layer=<id>` keeps one layer.

One note by name (URL-encode it; entity notes are named by path, such as `entities/src/app.ts`), with its graph relations: each `{ name, predicate, direction }` edge the note takes part in. `?layer=<id>` reads it from that layer only, for a name an arc layer shares with the workspace; without it the first layer that holds the name answers, workspace first.
The dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) that have a daily log.
One day's episodic log: each entry's time, provenance class, text and the session that wrote it when known.

400.description: The date is not `YYYY-MM-DD`.

get.summary: This server process's memory mutations, oldest first, capped at 128: each entry's op, time and file deltas with before and after content and hashes. Any entry can be reverted.

post.summary: Undo one ledger entry. `outcome` is `reverted` when every file still matched the entry's recorded result, or `needs-rebase` when something edited a file since; a rebase touches nothing.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No ledger entry has that id.

post.summary: Search memory the way the agent's recall does: lexical, semantic and graph legs ranked per hit. With `arc`, that arc's layer is searched on top of the workspace and boosted.

400.description: The body is not `{ query, arc? }`.

get.summary: An arc waiting to close: the notes it distilled (`candidates`, each with whether it meets the delivery bar and why not), its open `questions`, the sweep of its live sessions, the `successor` arc carried questions go to, and `decisions` so far. Every candidate and question needs a choice before the close can finish.

200.description: The digest, or the inert shape when the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No review is staged for that arc.

post.summary: Decide one distilled note: `deliver` promotes it into workspace memory when the arc closes (refused with 409 when it is below the bar), `leave` keeps it in the arc's archive.

400.description: The body is not `{ choice: "deliver" | "leave" }`.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No review is staged for that arc, or it has no such candidate.

409.description: The note is below the delivery bar.

post.summary: Decide one open question by title: `resolve` closes it, `carry` moves it to the newest other active arc (409 when there is none), `drop` closes it unanswered.

400.description: The body is not `{ title, choice: "resolve" | "carry" | "drop" }`.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No review is staged for that arc, or it has no such question.

409.description: No other active arc can carry the question.

post.summary: Decide every candidate at once: each eligible note is marked `deliver`, each below the bar `leave`. `delivered` counts the notes marked for delivery.

200.description: How many candidates will be delivered.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No review is staged for that arc.

post.summary: Close the arc with the decisions made so far. `kind` says what happened: `closed` (notes delivered, bound sessions released), `undecided` (`items` still need a choice), `wedged` (`sessions` did not flush their memory; `force: true` closes past them) or `pending`.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

404.description: No review is staged for that arc.

post.summary: Switch the model this session talks to from its next prompt on. The reference is resolved against the configured providers, the session's agent is rebuilt over the same history, and the choice is written to the session so a later open keeps it. A `session.state` envelope follows.

reference.description: `provider/model`, or a bare model name when only one provider offers it.

400.description: The body is not `{ reference }`, or the reference did not resolve: `code` carries the resolution failure (`unknown-model`, `unknown-provider`, `ambiguous`, `unavailable-credential`, …) and `failure` its detail.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

post.summary: Turn extended thinking on or off for this session's next prompts. Binary, not levelled. Recorded in the session; a `session.state` envelope follows.

400.description: The body is not `{ on: boolean }`.

post.summary: Set the reasoning effort for this session's next prompts, or `null` to return to the provider's default. Recorded in the session; a `session.state` envelope follows.

400.description: The body is not `{ level: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max" | null }`.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first. Only returning to the default needs an idle session.

post.summary: Fold the older part of the conversation into a summary now, keeping the recent turns verbatim. `focus` steers what the summary keeps. The session continues over the shorter context; a `session.state` envelope follows.

200.description: `{ compacted, notices }`: the compaction entry written, or `null` with a notice when there was nothing to fold.

400.description: The body is not `{ focus?: string }`.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

post.summary: Take back the last prompt: the conversation moves to just before it, its text comes back in `prompt` so a client can offer it for editing, and the files the turn changed are put back to the checkpoint taken before it. One undo is staged at a time; the next POST /redo cancels it. The undo is written to the session log as a `restore` entry, as POST /restore writes one, so a reopen finds the session rewound and POST /redo still takes it back after a server restart. With no prompt on the path, undoes the last file checkpoint alone. A `session.state` envelope follows.

200.description: `{ prompt: { entryId, text } | null, filesNote, undoable, redoable }`.

404.description: No session has that id. Or `{ error: "nothing to undo" }`.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

post.summary: Cancel the staged undo, restoring the transcript and the files, or redo the last file checkpoint when nothing is staged. A `session.state` envelope follows.

404.description: No session has that id. Or `{ error: "nothing to redo" }`.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

post.summary: Restore the session to just before one of its turns in one step, where POST /undo takes back one turn per call: the conversation moves to before that turn's prompt, and the workspace files go back to the checkpoint taken before the first change any turn from there on made (untouched when none of them changed a file, or with checkpoints off). One `restore` entry records it in the session log, `{ turn, from, files, redo }` with `redo` the snapshot of the files from before they went back, so a reopen finds the session where the restore left it and, even after a server restart, POST /redo can still put the files back. The answer says what changed: the turn's `prompt`, handed back so a client can offer it for editing; `undoneTurns`, how many turns left the active path; and `files`, every file the restore put back with the lines it `added` and `deleted`. Staged like an undo: the next POST /redo takes the whole restore back, files and conversation, and records a `restore-undone` entry so a reopen agrees. `session.state`, `session.tree` (reason `leaf`, naming the recorded entry) and, when files moved, `changes.updated` follow.

turn.description: The turn to restore to just before: its prompt's 1-based place among the prompts on the session's active path.

200.description: `{ turn, prompt: { entryId, text }, leafId, undoneTurns, files: [{ path, added, deleted }], filesNote, undoable, redoable }`; `leafId` is the recorded entry.

400.description: The body is not `{ turn }` with a positive integer.

404.description: No session has that id. Or `{ error: "no turn N on this session's path" }`.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

get.summary: What `POST /sessions/{id}/restore` would do for `?turn=N`, without doing it, so a client can ask before it acts: the turn's `prompt`, how many turns would leave the active path (`undoneTurns`), every file the restore would put back with the lines it would `add` and `delete` (`files`, empty when no turn from there on changed a file or checkpoints are off), and `others`: the sessions of this workspace other than this one whose turns touched any of those files after that turn began, each as `{ sessionId, title, paths }`, so the question can name the work a restore would take from them. A restore resets the whole workspace to the checkpoint, theirs included. `others` comes from the turns those sessions settled (their `turn_facts`) plus the turn a live one is running now; edits made outside keywork are in `files` but never in `others`.

200.description: `{ turn, prompt: { entryId, text }, undoneTurns, files: [{ path, added, deleted }], others: [{ sessionId, title, paths }] }`.

400.description: `turn` is not a positive integer.

404.description: No session has that id. Or `{ error: "no turn N on this session's path" }`.

get.summary: How full the model's context window is, as one reading every surface shows: `used` tokens of everything the next request carries (the sum of `parts` less `free`) against the `window`, with the points at which a memory flush (`flushAt`) and a compaction (`compactAt`) happen on the same axis. keywork's settler holds its reserves against the conversation, so the two lines sit at the window less the reserve plus what the system prompt and tool schemas take, and pass `window` when those outgrow the reserve. `basis` says where `used` comes from: `reported` once the provider has reported usage for the conversation so far (its count, plus an estimate of what arrived since), `estimated` from the text alone before that or after the history was rewritten, as a compaction, a flush, an undo or a forget does, so the reading right after any of them is a fresh measure of the shorter history and never the provider's older count. `declared` says whether the window came from keywork.json or is assumed. `parts` splits the same total, each as `{ tokens, basis }`: `system` (keywork's prompt and the configured prompts), `tools` (the tool schemas), `injected` (project instructions, the repo map, memory and extension context riding in the prompt), `conversation`, and `free` (the room left in the window). A part's `basis` is `reported` when it rests on what the provider reported for the last request, plus an estimate of what arrived since, and `estimated` when it comes from the text alone; the provider never splits its count, so `system`, `tools` and `injected` are always estimated. `thresholds` repeats `flushAt` and `compactAt` for clients that draw them across the parts.

200.description: `ContextReading & { fullness, flushDue, compactionDue, basis: "reported" | "estimated", parts: { system, tools, injected, conversation, free }, thresholds: { flushAt, compactAt } }`, each part `{ tokens, basis: "reported" | "estimated" }`.

get.summary: What the session has spent under `keywork serve`, this process and the ones before it: each turn's usage is written on its assistant message in the session log, so a restart picks the totals back up. Token `usage`, the cost `rollup` in nanodollars with how many turns were priced, metered or unpriced, a `basis` line saying how honest the number is, the last `cacheMiss` if the provider reported one in this process, and the same split per model under `models`, which lists only models that ran at least one turn.

200.description: `{ rollup, usage, basis, cacheMiss?, models: [{ reference, turns, usage, rollup }] }`.

post.summary: Render the session as a self-contained HTML page. `scope: "path"` (default) renders the active conversation; `"tree"` renders every branch. Without `out` the page is the response body; with `out`, a file or directory inside the workspace, the page is written there.

out.description: A file or directory inside the workspace scope.

201.description: `{ file }`: where the page was written.

400.description: The body is not `{ scope?: "path" | "tree", out?: string }`.

403.description: `out` escapes the workspace scope.

post.summary: Give the session a title. A title set this way is pinned: the automatic titler that names a session from its first exchange will not replace it. A `session.state` envelope follows.

400.description: The body is not `{ title: string }`.

post.summary: Switch the permission preset for this whole server process: `careful` asks before every core tool, `standard` follows the configured rules, `open` allows every core tool. Loosening (moving right in that order, or leaving a custom config) needs `confirmed: true`. The choice is saved to the user config and every live session sees a `gate.preset` event.

400.description: The body is not `{ name: "careful" | "standard" | "open", confirmed?: true }`.

409.description: Loosening needs `confirmed: true`.

501.description: This server was started without a preset switch.

get.summary: The workspace this server was launched for. `anchor` is its root and where the root came from: `declaration` when a `.keywork/workspace.json` was found walking up from the launch directory, `git` when a repository root was, `launch` when neither and the launch directory itself is the root. `identity` is the key its sessions and tickets are filed under (the same value as this document's `info.workspace.identity`). When a declaration exists, `declared` is true and `name`, `declarationFile`, `contextDirs` (extra folders the agent's tools and memory may reach), `missingContextDirs`, `focusDirs` (subtrees the workspace is about) and the memory `vault` describe it. `trust` is the user's standing decision for this root and `readiness` folds the two together: `ready` (trusted and declared), `undeclared` (trusted, no declaration yet), `undecided` (no decision yet, so nothing runs with project access) or `refused` (marked untrusted).

post.summary: Trust the served workspace and set it up, exactly what `/init` in the terminal and `keywork trust` do: the decision is written for this root and no other (the body is ignored, so no path can be smuggled in) to the user's trust store, and `.keywork/workspace.json` plus the memory vault are created when missing. Trust is read when a server composes, so `keywork serve` composes itself again before it answers: the project's config, permissions, MCP servers, arcs and bots load, open sessions close (a running turn is interrupted and keeps what it had) and reopen on their next request, pending asks are refused, and the URL, the token, the ticket and the event stream stay as they were. `recomposed: true` says that happened, and `GET /permissions` reflects trust as soon as the answer arrives; `surface.changed` fires with `kind: "workspaces"` and, after a recompose, `kind: "permissions"`. `reopens: true` says this host cannot recompose itself (an embedded host) and must be restarted before the decision takes effect; a client that owns the process restarts it. Already trusted is not an error and answers both false. This route never untrusts and never forgets a decision.

200.description: `{ trusted: true, root, vault, reopens, recomposed }`; `root` names the directory the decision covers.

400.description: The root is a home directory or a filesystem root, which would trust everything beneath it.

409.description: The root is marked untrusted; only `keywork trust` in a terminal reverses that.

get.summary: One directory level of the workspace, for a file browser. `path` is relative to the workspace root (empty or absent for the root itself; an absolute path reaches a linked context folder). Each entry is a `file` or a `dir`, directories first, then by name. Entries that a `.gitignore` between the root and this directory ignores are returned with `ignored: true` rather than dropped, so a browser can dim them. Dotfiles are left out unless `hidden=true`, and come flagged `hidden: true` when included. Every path is confined to the scope the agent's tools get: `..`, symlinks that leave it and anything outside the workspace answer 403.

403.description: The path escapes the workspace scope.

get.summary: A slice of one text file as UTF-8: the bytes `[from, to)` of it, the whole file when neither is given. At most 1 MiB comes back per request; when the slice was cut short, `truncated` is true and `to` says where it stopped, so the next request starts there. `bytes` is the whole file's size. A clipped tool result's `spill.elidedFrom` and `elidedTo` are the `from` and `to` that open the clipped range. Files over 20 MiB are refused, a slice holding a NUL byte is refused as binary, and `path` is confined exactly as for `/tree`.

400.description: `from` or `to` is not a non-negative integer.

403.description: The path escapes the workspace scope.

413.description: The file is over the 20 MiB cap.

415.description: The slice holds a NUL byte: a binary file.

get.summary: Every configured MCP server (a tool provider the agent can call) with its live status: `state` is `connected`, `connecting` or `down`, `enabled` is the user's switch, `toolCount` is how many tools it currently offers, `transport` is `stdio` or `http`, and `lastError` says why it is down when it is. `surface.changed` with `kind: "mcp"` fires whenever any of this changes. An empty list means no servers are configured.

503.description: This host serves no MCP registry.

post.summary: Drop the server's connection and open a fresh one, re-enabling it if it was off. Answers once the server has settled, with its new status.

200.description: The server's status after the restart.

404.description: No MCP server has that name.

503.description: The registry is stopping, or this host serves none.

post.summary: Switch a server on or off. Off disconnects it and withdraws its tools until it is switched on again; on reconnects it. Answers once the server has settled.

200.description: The server's status after the switch.

400.description: The body is not `{ on: boolean }`.

404.description: No MCP server has that name.

503.description: The registry is stopping, or this host serves none.

get.summary: The names of the tools a server currently offers; empty while it is down.

404.description: No MCP server has that name.

503.description: This host serves no MCP registry.

get.summary: Every arc in the workspace: a named stretch of work that sessions bind to and that keeps its own memory layer until it closes. Each arc carries its `slug`, `status` (`active` or `archived`), `created` time and how many `sessions` are bound to it. `ordinals` numbers the arcs by creation order so a client can give each a stable colour. Arcs need a trusted workspace with memory.

403.description: The workspace is untrusted, so there are no arcs.

post.summary: Open a new active arc named by `slug` (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens). Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "arcs"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ slug }` or the slug is not valid.

403.description: The workspace is untrusted.

409.description: An arc with that slug already exists.

post.summary: Close an arc: its live sessions are swept for memory, and its notes and open questions are distilled for review. `kind: "closed"` means it closed at once, delivering `delivered` notes and releasing `released` sessions; `kind: "pending"` means `candidates` notes and `questions` are waiting at the airlock (see `GET /arcs/{slug}/airlock`) and the arc stays open until they are decided. `direction` is an optional sentence steering what the close should keep.

403.description: The workspace is untrusted.

409.description: The arc is not active.

post.summary: Archive an arc without distilling anything: its sessions are released and its layer is kept only as an archive. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "arcs"`.

403.description: The workspace is untrusted.

post.summary: Have an arc wear a theme, or none with `theme: null`. The theme is recorded on the arc itself, so every client dressing the arc's panes wears the same one; `theme` must name a theme `GET /themes` serves. Answers the arc as `GET /arcs` lists it. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "arcs"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ theme: string | null }`.

403.description: The workspace is untrusted.

409.description: The arc is not active, or no theme has that name.

post.summary: Bind a session to an arc, or release it with `slug: null`. The binding is recorded in the session's log and answers as the session's whole binding (`arc`, `bot`). From then on the session's memory writes go to the arc's layer and its recall searches that layer first.

200.description: The session's binding after the change.

400.description: The body is not `{ slug: string | null }` or the slug is not valid.

post.summary: Have a session run as a bot (a named role with its own prompt, tool allowance and memory layer), or as no bot with `name: null`. A live session's agent is rebuilt as that bot before the answer, and a `model` the bot declares becomes the session's model, so the next prompt runs as the bot. Refused while a turn is running, because the running agent cannot be swapped mid-turn. Answers as the session's whole binding (`arc`, `bot`); a `session.state` envelope follows.

200.description: The session's binding after the change.

400.description: The body is not `{ name: string | null }` or the name is not valid.

409.description: A turn is running.

get.summary: Every bot defined for this workspace and this user: its `name`, display `sigil`, where it was defined (`source` is `project` or `user`), its `description`, the `model` it prefers and its `learning` policy, plus how many `sessions` have run as it, when it was `lastUsed` and what those sessions cost when known.

post.summary: Define a new bot: writes `.keywork/bots/<slug>/bot.md` in the workspace (`scope: "project"`, needs a trusted workspace) or under the user's home (`scope: "user"`), with `purpose` as its description. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "bots"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ slug, scope, purpose? }` or the slug is not valid.

403.description: A project bot was asked for in an untrusted workspace.

409.description: A bot with that name already exists.

get.summary: The workspaces that share this root: the default one (no `slug`) and every named one under `.keywork/workspaces/<slug>/`. Each says whether it is `declared` (set up on disk), whether it is the `current` one this server runs, how many memory `notes` it holds, its `focusDirs`, how many `sessions` it has and when it was `lastUsed` (epoch milliseconds).

post.summary: Create a named workspace over this root: a separate declaration and memory vault under `.keywork/workspaces/<slug>/`. The new workspace is not opened; `POST /workspaces/use` does that. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "workspaces"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ slug }`, the slug is not valid, or it is the reserved word `default`.

409.description: A workspace with that slug already exists.

post.summary: Choose the workspace the next launch from this directory opens: a named one by `slug`, or the default with `slug: null`. A workspace is a separate identity with its own sessions and memory, so the running server cannot switch in place: `reopens: true` says a client that owns the server process must restart it, which then opens the chosen workspace.

400.description: The body is not `{ slug: string | null }`.

409.description: No workspace has that slug.

post.summary: Add a focus dir to a workspace (`default` names the default workspace): a subtree of the root the workspace is about, which memory recall and the sessions overview lean toward. `dir` is relative to the root or absolute and must be inside it; nothing here widens what the agent's tools may touch. Answers the dir as recorded. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "workspaces"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ dir }`.

409.description: The dir is not a directory, lies outside the root, is the root itself, or is already a focus dir; or the workspace is not declared.

post.summary: Remove a focus dir from a workspace (`default` names the default workspace); `dir` is the value `GET /workspaces` lists. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "workspaces"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ dir }`.

409.description: That dir is not a focus dir of the workspace, or the workspace is not declared.

get.summary: Every theme the server can hand a client whole: the curated gallery (keywork-night, keywork-day, and the Catppuccin, Nord, Gruvbox, Everforest, Kanagawa, Rosé Pine, Flexoki, matte-black, osaka-jade, ristretto, and whiplash themes) plus any closet theme, which replaces a gallery theme of the same name. Each record is complete: name, appearance, tokens, density, gap, chromeWeight, instruments, and always terminal (the ANSI 16), syntax, diff, selection, and cursor, filled by keywork's derivation rule where the theme leaves one out, so every client paints from the same colors. Every theme served has passed keywork's contrast floors and reads in its declared appearance (dark ink on a light ground or light on dark on every measured pair), so a client need not re-validate. `pair` names the opposite-appearance twin when there is one, so a client following the OS swaps between a matched light and dark. `active` is the configured startup theme. `placeholders` names themes the terminal derives from its own environment (`system`, from the terminal's colors); a client fills those from its own surface so both surfaces list the same names.

The session's whole entry log as the engine stores it, for a client that draws the conversation tree itself. `entries` is every entry in file order, each with its `id` and `parentId`; `message` entries carry their message whole, and the rest (`compaction`, `branch_summary`, `label`, `session_info`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`, `effort_change`, `context_edit`, `binding`, `custom`, `custom_message`) carry their own fields. A memory flush is a `custom_message` with `customType: "memory_flush"` whose `content` is the prompt keywork sent, followed by the reply as an `assistant` message entry; it is not a prompt and starts no turn. `labels` maps entry ids to the label in force, `leafId` is the entry the next message will follow, and `activePath` lists the ids from the root to that leaf. `journal` lists the ids of the entries kept only as evidence, which never reach the model and are not part of the conversation: the `custom` entries recording permission asks and decisions, context injections, memory decisions, shell resets, session grants and each settled turn's facts (`turn_facts`). A tree, a transcript or an export leaves them out, or folds them into the row they explain. Folding the flat log into a tree is the client's job (parent links suffice).

200.description: `{ sessionId, name?, leafId, entries, labels, activePath, journal }`.

post.summary: Start a new session from one entry of this one: the path from the root to `entryId` is copied into a fresh session whose header records the file it was forked from as `parentSession`. This session is untouched. A `session.tree` envelope with `reason: "fork"` and `forkedTo` follows on this session.

201.description: `{ sessionId }`: the new session, readable at GET /sessions/{sessionId}.

400.description: The body is not `{ entryId: string }`.

404.description: No session has that id, or no entry in it has that id.

post.summary: Name an entry so a branch is easy to find again, or pass `null` to remove the name. The label is written to the session as its own entry, so it survives a restart. A `session.tree` envelope with `reason: "label"` follows.

400.description: The body is not `{ entryId: string, label: string | null }`.

404.description: No session has that id, or no entry in it has that id.

post.summary: Move the session's leaf to `entryId` (or to the empty root with `null`) without forking: the next prompt continues from there, as a new branch if the entry already has children. The session's agent is rebuilt over the shorter path, the same move POST /undo makes without putting files back. Needs an idle session. A `session.tree` envelope with `reason: "leaf"` and a `session.state` envelope follow.

entryId.description: `null` moves to the empty root, before the first entry.

400.description: The body is not `{ entryId: string | null }`.

404.description: No session has that id, or no entry in it has that id.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

get.summary: Every file this session's turns touched that differs now from the checkpoint taken before the session's first change (`baseline` names it: `session start`). Files only another session or a person outside keywork changed are not listed, so two sessions on one workspace each see their own work. A file both touched shows its net change, theirs included. Each entry carries the path relative to the workspace root, the lines `added` and `deleted`, and `turn`, the 1-based ordinal of the session's turn that last touched it. A settled turn's files are the ones its `turn_facts` journal entry froze when it settled, so the list reads the same after a restart; the turn still running is measured from its own checkpoint. The list is recomputed on every call; `changes.updated` says when to call again.

200.description: `{ baseline, files: [{ path, added, deleted, turn? }] }`.

409.description: `{ error: "no baseline" }`: checkpoints are off for this server, so there is no session start to diff against.

get.summary: Both sides of one changed file, for a client that renders the diff itself: `before` as it was at the baseline and `after` as it is in the working tree, each `null` when the file did not exist on that side (`note` says `new` or `deleted`; `unreadable` when neither side could be read). A file with a NUL byte on either side answers `note: "binary"` with no text. Each side is capped at 1 MiB of UTF-8, cut on a character boundary, and `truncated` says when a side was cut. `path` is the query parameter, relative to the workspace root as GET /sessions/{id}/changes lists it, and is confined to the workspace scope.

400.description: No `path` query parameter.

403.description: The path escapes the workspace scope.

409.description: `{ error: "no baseline" }`: checkpoints are off for this server, so there is no session start to diff against.

413.description: The working file is over the 20 MiB cap GET /files applies.

get.summary: The keeper's verdicts on the hunks of this session's changes, oldest first: every `keywork.review.verdict` entry on the session's active path, each `{ index, entryId, at, path, header, digest, verdict }`. `path` is the changed file as GET /sessions/{id}/changes lists it, `header` the hunk's unified range line (`@@ -a,b +c,d @@`), `digest` eight hex characters over the hunk's removed and added lines (the stable reference a quote in the thread carries as `hunk <digest>`, which survives the hunk moving when an earlier hunk is dropped), and `verdict` one of `keep`, `drop`, `ask`. The same hunk judged twice appears twice; the last word stands, so a client folds the trail by `path` and `digest`. `index` is the position in `GET /sessions/{id}` `messages` the entry was written before, where `verdicts` lists the same marks for a transcript that replays the trail as notices. Since contract 1.18.

200.description: `{ verdicts: [{ index, entryId, at, path, header, digest, verdict }] }`.

post.summary: Record the keeper's verdict on one hunk: `keep`, `drop` or `ask`. The verdict is written to the session as a journal-only `keywork.review.verdict` entry (never a prompt, never in the model context, so no turn starts) and the same write emits one `extension.notice` from the `review` extension, `message` the trail line a transcript draws (`<verdict> · <path> <header> · hunk <digest>`) and `detail: { verdict: <the mark>, entryId }`, so a watching console updates its marks and its conversation at once. A verdict of `ask` parks the hunk as something waiting on the keeper until a later `keep` or `drop` on the same `path` and `digest`. The body names the hunk exactly as GET /sessions/{id}/changes/verdicts lists it. Since contract 1.18.

201.description: The mark as GET /sessions/{id}/changes/verdicts lists it.

400.description: The body is not `{ path, header, digest, verdict }` with a unified hunk header, an eight-hex digest and a verdict of keep, drop or ask.

501.description: `{ error: "verdicts are not wired" }`: this server's host records no hunk verdicts yet, so the verdict was not written.

get.summary: Sessions in the trash, newest first, summarized exactly as `GET /sessions` summarizes a live one.

delete.summary: Empty the trash. `purged` counts the sessions deleted. There is no undo.

post.summary: Move a trashed session back into the session directory, log and spills together. It lists again at once. Fires `session.restored`.

404.description: Nothing in the trash has that id.

delete.summary: Delete one trashed session for good. There is no undo.

404.description: Nothing in the trash has that id.

get.summary: What this server allows beyond the configured rules, so every grant is visible: `{ trusted, bundle, workspace, session }`. `bundle` is the fixed read-only posture a trusted workspace gets (empty when untrusted), `workspace` the grants recorded by `scope: "workspace"` answers and workspace grants, and `session` the grants from `scope: "session"` answers and session grants, keyed by session id, for the sessions open in this server process (a session's journaled grants come back when it reopens). Configured rules decide first; where they are silent, session grants, then workspace grants, then the bundle decide. `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"` fires whenever this answer would change.

post.summary: Record one rule for every session of this workspace before any call asks for it, exactly where a `scope: "workspace"` answer to an ask records it. Only a rule an answered ask could have recorded is taken, or a whole MCP server: a `bash` rule in the shape an ask derives (`npm run *`, `git push *`, a delete only as its exact command), an MCP tool with resource `*`, or every tool of one MCP server as one rule, action `mcp` with resource `<server>__*`. A trusted-workspace setup can accept its proposals this way, one rule at a time. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ rule: { action, resource, effect: "allow" } }`.

409.description: The workspace is not trusted, or the rule is neither one an answered ask would record nor a whole MCP server: a `write` or `edit` rule, a pattern over tool names, an `mcp` rule over part of a server or over several, a wildcard over a delete or `git branch -D`, any force push, hard reset, `git clean` or discarding checkout, or any other shape (`error` names what an answer would record instead, when there is one).

post.summary: Record one rule for that session before any call asks for it, exactly where a `scope: "session"` answer records it; the session is opened if it was not. Under `keywork serve` every change to the grants of a session is written to its log as a `session_grants` snapshot and a reopen adopts the latest one, so the grant outlives the server process. The same rules are taken as for POST /permissions/workspace/grant. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ rule: { action, resource, effect: "allow" } }`.

409.description: The workspace is not trusted, or the rule is neither one an answered ask would record nor a whole MCP server: a `write` or `edit` rule, a pattern over tool names, an `mcp` rule over part of a server or over several, a wildcard over a delete or `git branch -D`, any force push, hard reset, `git clean` or discarding checkout, or any other shape (`error` names what an answer would record instead, when there is one).

post.summary: Remove one workspace grant, so the call it covered asks again in every session of this workspace. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ rule: { action, resource, effect: "allow" } }`.

404.description: No workspace grant matches that rule.

post.summary: Remove one grant a `scope: "session"` answer recorded for that session, so the call it covered asks again there, after a server restart too (the revoke is journaled like a grant). Other sessions and the workspace grants are untouched. Fires `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"`.

400.description: The body is not `{ rule: { action, resource, effect: "allow" } }`.

404.description: That session holds no grant matching the rule.

post.summary: Let a session run without a person at the keyboard for what a `session` answer already covers. While quiet is on, the gate grants a call itself when a `session` answer to its ask would record rules, none of them a blanket `<program> *` and no part of the command destructive (a delete, `git branch -D`, a force push, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, a discarding checkout). Those rules join the session's grants and the decision reads `gate.permission` with `gate: "quiet"` and `scope: "session"`, so no client mistakes it for a person's answer; no `gate.ask` fires for it. Everything else still asks: `write` and `edit`, a call a grant could not remember, blanket and destructive commands, and the write-capable forms the trusted reads hold back. Turning quiet off revokes nothing it granted. The posture is written to the session log as a `quiet` entry, so a reopened session keeps it; `session.state` carries it as `quiet`, `GET /permissions` lists quiet sessions under `quiet`, and `surface.changed` with `kind: "permissions"` fires when it moves. `keywork run` and every other headless gate never go quiet.

400.description: The body is not `{ on: boolean }`.

post.summary: Run the memory flush now instead of waiting for the context to reach the flush line: the session's model is asked what in this conversation is worth keeping across sessions, and what it names goes to the daily log (the bound arc's, when there is one; lines about a bot's own craft go to that bot). The flush prompt and its reply join the conversation, exactly as with the flush the settler runs after a turn. `flushed` is how many messages that added, 0 when nothing ran, and `notices` says what happened in keywork's words. A workspace that is not trusted has inert memory, so nothing is flushed there. `session.settled` with `phase: "requested"` follows with the same `flushed` and `notices`, then a `session.state` envelope.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

post.summary: Take one prompt or one tool result out of what the model sees, or rewrite it, while the transcript keeps the original: what the terminal's /forget does. `entryId` names a user prompt or a tool result message on the session's active path, with the ids `GET /sessions/{id}/entries` lists. Without `replacement` the model stops seeing it; with one, the model sees that text in its place. The edit is written to the session log as a `context_edit` entry, which becomes the leaf, and the session continues over the edited context. Needs an idle session. `session.state` and `session.tree` (`reason: "leaf"`, naming the edit) follow.

replacement.description: What the model sees instead. Absent, the entry leaves the model's context.

200.description: `{ edit }`: the `context_edit` entry written, with its `targetId` and `replacement`.

400.description: The body is not `{ entryId, replacement?: string }`.

404.description: No session has that id, or `{ error: "no prompt or tool result on this session's path has that id" }`.

409.description: A turn is running; wait for it or abort it first.

post.summary: The dry run of forgetting everything one source put in memory; it touches nothing. `plan` lists exactly what an apply would remove: the notes the source wrote (each with its first line), the checkpoint anchors they carry, every graph edge that touches them, the recall and citation lines naming them in the curation audit, for a session its daily entries, and the inbox items still staged from that source (`staged`: each with its `id`, `kind`, `target`, addressee `for` and first line); `counts` sums each list, `kept` names notes a session only shares with another session and why they stay, and `digest` fingerprints the whole plan for `POST /memory/forget/apply`. A `craft:<slug>` source reads that creature's own layer.

source.description: Where the memory came from: `session:<id>`, `creature:<slug>` (another creature's messages), `web:<origin>`, `workshop:<id>` (a workshop's output), `craft:<slug>` (a creature's whole craft section) or `craft:<slug>/<note>` (one craft note).

200.description: `{ plan }`: `{ source, digest, counts, notes, anchors, edges, citations, entries, staged, kept }`.

400.description: The body is not `{ source }`, or the source is not one of the kinds named.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

501.description: `{ error: "this node does not serve forget by source yet" }`.

503.description: Memory is not served by this host.

post.summary: Forget a source for real, after its dry run: removes exactly the notes, daily entries, staged inbox items and audit citation lines `POST /memory/forget/preview` listed under `digest`, in one ledger entry that `POST /memory/ledger/{id}/revert` undoes byte for byte, and appends a `forgot <source> · <counts>` line to the curation audit. If the vault moved since the dry run (a note was added, edited or removed) nothing is touched and the answer is 409.

source.description: Where the memory came from: `session:<id>`, `creature:<slug>` (another creature's messages), `web:<origin>`, `workshop:<id>` (a workshop's output), `craft:<slug>` (a creature's whole craft section) or `craft:<slug>/<note>` (one craft note).

digest.description: The `digest` of the dry run the keeper read; anything else is refused.

200.description: `{ forgot }`: `{ source, counts, ledgerId? }`; no `ledgerId` when nothing was there to forget.

400.description: The body is not `{ source, digest }`, or the source is not one of the kinds named.

403.description: Memory is inert: the workspace is untrusted.

409.description: The dry run is stale; run it again and apply its new digest.

501.description: `{ error: "this node does not serve forget by source yet" }`.

503.description: Memory is not served by this host.

post.summary: Move one prompt waiting behind the running turn to another place in the queue, as the terminal does with alt+arrow while it edits the queue. `itemId` is the prompt's `id` from `queue.changed`. Steered prompts always run before queued ones, so a move that would put a queued prompt ahead of a steered one, or a steered one behind a queued one, is refused. `queue.changed` follows with the new order.

to.description: The prompt's new 0-based place in the queue, as `queue.changed` lists it.

200.description: `{ queued }`: the whole queue after the move, as `queue.changed` carries it.

400.description: The body is not `{ to }` with a non-negative integer.

404.description: No session has that id, or `{ error: "no queued prompt has that id" }`.

409.description: `to` is past the end of the queue, or the move would cross a steered prompt.

delete.summary: Drop one prompt waiting behind the running turn before it runs. `itemId` is the prompt's `id` from `queue.changed`, which follows without it.

200.description: `{ queued }`: the whole queue after the prompt left it.

404.description: No session has that id, or `{ error: "no queued prompt has that id" }`.

get.summary: A slice of the full output a tool result clipped, read from the session's own spill directory beside its log and never from the workspace, so the tool jail does not apply and a spill stays readable wherever the workspace scope ends. `spillId` is `spill.id` from the tool result (on `tool.finished` and in the stored message); only a spill this session's log references is served. Without `from` and `to` the slice is exactly the clipped range the reference carries, `[elidedFrom, elidedTo)`; with either, it is the bytes `[from, to)` of the whole output. At most 1 MiB comes back per request: when the slice was cut short, `truncated` is true and `to` says where it stopped. `bytes` is the whole output's size and `spill` the reference itself. A slice holding a NUL byte is refused as binary.

200.description: `{ spill, bytes, from, to, text, truncated, encoding }`.

400.description: `from` or `to` is not a non-negative integer.

404.description: No session has that id, or `{ error: "no spill has that id in this session" }`, or the spill file is gone.

415.description: The slice holds a NUL byte.

get.summary: Every creature in this workspace: a bot (`GET /bots`) whose directory also holds a `creature.json`. Each row carries the bot's `slug` and `sigil`, the keeper's `name` for it, when it was `created`, its body (`skin`, `seed`) for the habitat, its `workshop` (`host` for the bare node, else a workshop id), its model policy `models` (`strong`, `loop`, `decide`, `vision`, each `inherit` or `{ provider, model }`), the id of its `conversation` once one exists (`null` before the first `GET /creatures/{slug}` opens it) how many live `threads` it has, and `paused`, when the keeper paused it (`POST /creatures/{slug}/pause`) or `null` while it runs. A bot without a `creature.json` is not listed; a creature with the host workshop and `inherit` everywhere behaves exactly as that bot would.

post.summary: Make a creature: writes `.keywork/bots/<slug>/bot.md` byte for byte as `POST /bots` would (so the creature is a bot first) and `creature.json` beside it, with the slug derived from `name` (REQ-003: the name stays editable in the file, the slug is its handle). `skin` defaults to the stead's first skin, every model class to `inherit`; the seed is drawn here. Where it works: `workshop` names an existing workshop id or `host` (the bare node, the default), or `substrate` (`sbx`, `compose` or `host`, as `GET /workshops/substrates` lists them) raises a new workshop for it first, exactly as `POST /workshops` would, records its id, then starts it as `POST /workshops/{id}/start` would, so the workshop reads `running` before the creature's first turn; the two are exclusive. A workshop that will not start leaves the creature made: its first tool call starts it (one line in that tool's output says so), and when it still cannot, the tool answers why in words and the creature tells the keeper. A substrate this node does not support is refused before anything is written, and a workshop raised for a creature that then cannot be written is removed again. The creature composes its one introduction sentence at creation and keeps it in `creature.json`, where the keeper can edit it. Needs a trusted workspace, as project bots do. Nothing is opened yet: the conversation is created lazily by the first `GET /creatures/{slug}`. A `creature.changed` event with `change: "created"` follows, after `workshop.changed` when one was raised and before its `change: "started"`.

201.description: The new creature's summary, as `GET /creatures` lists it.

400.description: The body is not a creature draft, or the name makes no slug.

409.description: A bot already has that slug, or the workspace is not trusted.

502.description: The substrate's own command failed while raising the workshop; `error` says what it said.

503.description: This host serves no creatures, serves no workshops while a substrate was named, or does not support that substrate (`error` says why).

get.summary: One creature with what a console opened mid-day needs before the first event: the summary row, its `introduction`, the `conversation` id (opened now, bound to the bot and tagged `kind: conversation`, when the creature had none; it is never trashed while the creature exists), its live `threads` newest first, each `{ id, kind: thread | routine, title, state, children, lastActivityAt }` with `state` one of `working`, `waiting` (an ask is pending), `back`, `blocked` or `paused` and `children` the sub-agents rolled up into it, the `nextRun` of its routines (`{ routineId, at }` or `null`), today's `usage` (`{ date, sessions, costNanos }`, `costNanos` `null` when no ledger has priced it, never 0) and the `routines` directory under the creature. Live state afterward rides the session events on /events; thread summaries reach the conversation as prompts whose `origin` is `{ kind: "creature", creature, thread }`.

patch.summary: Change what the keeper may change about a creature in `creature.json`: its `name` (the slug stays its handle; an introduction still in the words it was composed with follows the new name, one the keeper edited is kept), its `body` (`skin`, `seed`), its model policy `models` (only the classes named change; `inherit` hands a class back to the workspace and user policy), `cloudFallback` and `inbound`, who may message it over the mesh (`nobody`, `paired` for creatures on this machine or a paired one, or `{ named: [...] }`, creature slugs optionally pinned with `@machine`; every summary carries it, `paired` when never set; see `POST /mesh/messages`). The file is validated as a whole before it is written. Answers the summary as `GET /creatures` lists it; a `creature.changed` event with `change: "updated"` follows.

200.description: The creature's summary after the change.

400.description: The body changes nothing or is not a creature patch.

delete.summary: Remove a creature in two steps, as REQ-090 asks. Without `?confirmed=true` nothing changes: the answer is 409 carrying `removal`, what `goes` (its `definition` directory with `bot.md` and `creature.json`, its `conversation` and `threads`, which move to the trash as `DELETE /sessions/{id}` would, how many of its `notes` are retired from its memory layer, how many `routines` files go with the directory, and its `workshop` unless `?keepWorkshop=true`) and what `stays` (the `workspace` with the keeper's own notes, and the kept `workshop`). With `?confirmed=true` the same listing is carried out in that order, threads first, the conversation last, the definition after them, and the answer is 200 with `removed: true` and the `removal` that happened. A `creature.changed` event with `change: "removed"` follows; the trashed sessions fire `session.removed` each.

200.description: `{ removed: true, removal }`: the creature is gone and `removal` says what went and what stayed.

400.description: The query is not `confirmed=true` and optionally `keepWorkshop=true|false`.

409.description: Not confirmed: `removal` lists what `goes` and what `stays` when it is.

get.summary: The keeper-would-approve report for this creature, as `keywork creatures report --json` prints it for the whole node but counted over the ledger rows tagged with this creature: `{ creature, gateId, mode: "shadow" | "enforce", enforced, ledgerPath, evidenceVersion?, rows, earlierRows, classes, gate?, auditRate, calibration, promotions, pendingReviews }`. Each class is `{ ruleClass, model?, rows, labelled, answered, agreement?, brier?, wouldAct, wrongActs, oneWayDoor, grade, gradeWord, gradeText }`. `calibration` holds one entry per model and rule class, `{ model, ruleClass, state, labelled, fitRows, heldOutRows, bar?, fitActs?, acts, sampleSize, agreement?, interval?, errors?, lowerBound?, review }`: the bar is fitted on the first 50 labelled answers and judged on the calls after them, `state` is `fitting`, `no-bar`, `collecting`, `awaiting-labels`, `accepted` or `rejected`, agreement and its 95% interval stay sealed until the planned sample is complete, and `review` counts the blind review (`drawn`, `answered`, `agreedWithGate`, `agreedWithMoment`, `deniedAtBar`) that samples answered asks at `auditRate`. `promotions` lists the rule classes the keeper handed over that cover this creature; with none, `mode` is `shadow`, `enforced` is false and every ask waits for the keeper. A one-way door is never promoted. A creature with no answered asks yet has `rows: 0` and no classes.

post.summary: The keeper hands one rule class of this creature's asks to `keeper.would-approve`. The body is `{ ruleClass }`, exactly one class as the report names it. The promotion is accepted only when that class's calibration for the model answering it now is `accepted`: the bar was fitted on the first 50 labelled answers, then the planned sample of the first 149 distinct held-out calls above it (at most 10 from one session) were each approved, so the exact one-sided 95% lower bound reaches the promised 98%, and the blind review denied no call above the bar. A one-way door, `all classes`, a class already promoted, or one short of its evidence is refused with a `sentence` saying what it needs. The promotion is a reversible record scoped to this creature, `{ ruleClass, model, evidenceVersion, bar, creature, sampleSize, errors, lowerBound, by: "keeper", at }`. Decided calls still log, still show as decided for you and can be overturned, a blind review still samples them at the audit rate, and `POST /creatures/{slug}/demote` hands the class back. Nothing is ever promoted without this call.

post.summary: The creature as an MCP server for an agent on this machine, over streamable HTTP with this server's token as the bearer (the loopback ticket): one JSON-RPC message per POST, answered as JSON (`202` and no body for a notification); no event stream and no session id. It speaks MCP `2026-07-28` (`server/discover`) and the 2025 revisions (`initialize`). Three tools: `ask` leaves the creature plain words (`{ text }`, up to 2000 characters) as one creature-origin line in its conversation, the `keywork.creature.report` entry creature mail uses, so it starts no turn and carries no approval, grant or configuration, and answers a `handle`; `ask { handle }` polls, returning the creature's first reply from the turn after the words landed, or that it has not answered yet. `status` answers `working`, `at the porch`, `back`, `idle` or `paused`. `deliveries` returns the report lines finished threads and chores delivered (`{ after?, limit? }`, oldest first). The creature's `inbound` policy gates every tool (`nobody` refuses, `paired` admits, `{ named }` admits only those creatures, never an agent); asks share the hourly limits of creature mail; every call is an audit row (`creature.ask`, `creature.status`, `creature.deliveries`) with its arguments only digested. Bad arguments, an unknown tool, or fields such as `approve` are JSON-RPC `-32602`.

The workspace answers it as `POST /creatures/{slug}/mcp` would, for a caller on that paired machine: the inbound policy, the shared limits and the audit row all name it. A node that keeps its tailnet listener in another process than its workspaces posts each arrival here, trying the next workspace on 404.

get.summary: The creature's chores, read again from its `routines/<id>.json` files (the files are the source; the node's SQLite journal is the index). Each row is `{ creature, id, file, routine, problem, grants: { posture, digest, needsAcceptance, accepted, acceptedAt }, schedule: { enabled, disabled, nextRunAt, consecutiveErrors, retryAt }, activeRunId, lastRun }`: `routine` is null and `problem` says why when a file does not parse; `schedule.nextRunAt` is the next planned start including the routine's deterministic stagger; `schedule.disabled` carries the reason when repeated failures turned the chore off.

One chore as `{ creature, id, file, routine, problem, grants: { posture, digest, needsAcceptance, accepted, acceptedAt }, schedule: { enabled, disabled, nextRunAt, consecutiveErrors, retryAt }, activeRunId, lastRun }`.

404.description: No creature has that slug, or it has no chore with that id.

put.summary: Write the chore's file and index it. The body is the routine file (`id` may be left out; the path names it). Triggers are `cron` (with an IANA `tz` and an optional `until`), `interval` (with an optional `until` instant), `at` (one instant), `file-watch` (paths or globs under the workspace, debounced), `webhook` (fired through `POST /hooks/{slug}/{id}` with the chore's token) and `event` (a bus event by name, with a `where` filter), and `manual`; since contract 1.17 for the last four beside the first two. A fired trigger is a stored assignment, never consent: every trigger parks the same way on an unaccepted grant set. A chore with `wake` is one the creature asked for itself with the schedule tool; the keeper removes it like any other. `tools` is `read-only` unless the chore declares `write` or `act` with a `grants` set, and the keeper must accept that set once (`POST .../accept`) before such a chore runs; nothing in this body can accept it. Putting a chore that repeated failures disabled back with `enabled: true` reinstates it.

id.description: The chore's name and its file name (routines/<id>.json).

title.description: What the keeper sees on the chore board.

instructions.description: The assignment the run is given; a stored assignment, never consent (RUN-033).

expr.description: When the chore fires, in the five-field cron form the keeper already reads.

tz.description: The IANA zone the expression is read in, so 9am stays 9am across DST (RUN-034).

until.description: The last day (inclusive, in tz) or instant the chore may fire (REQ-060).

minutes.description: Minutes between runs, counted from when the node first indexed the chore.

until.description: The instant after which the chore stops firing; a creature's paced wakeup expires so (RUN-048).

at.description: The one instant the chore fires: a one-shot, the shape of a creature's own wakeup (REQ-057).

paths.description: Paths or globs (*, **, ?) under the workspace root; nothing outside it is watched.

debounceMs.description: Changes inside this quiet window batch into one run (RUN-043).

maxBytes.description: The largest body the hook takes; a larger one is refused and never reaches a run.

name.description: The bus event that fires the chore, by exact name (for example routine.finished).

where.description: Payload fields, by dotted path, that must equal these values for the event to count.

debounceMs.description: Matching events inside this window batch into one run (RUN-043); 0 fires on each.

trigger.description: What starts a run: a time (cron, interval, at), an occurrence (file-watch, webhook, event) or the keeper (manual).

destination.description: Where the finished output goes: the conversation, a named thread or a file.

notify.description: When the keeper hears about a run that does not need them (RUN-046).

tools.description: The tool posture; write and act need the keeper to accept the grants once.

grants.description: The grant set a write or act chore asks for; anything outside it asks.

budget.description: Per-run ceilings; exceeding either ends the run blocked with the reason.

enabled.description: Whether the schedule fires at all.

wake.description: Present when the creature asked for this chore itself (REQ-057); the keeper cancels it like any chore.

requestedAt.description: When the creature asked for this wakeup with the schedule tool.

200.description: `{ routine, created: false }`: the chore was replaced.

201.description: `{ routine, created: true }`: the chore is new.

400.description: The body is not a valid routine, or its id differs from the path.

A run still in progress or parked refuses the new one, which is recorded as `skipped`. Answers `{ runId, creature, routineId, attempt, trigger, catchUp, firedAt, scheduledFor, status, sessionId, startedAt, endedAt, process, delivery, verified, reason, usage, cost, output, notify }`; `routine.fired` and `routine.finished` follow on the event stream.

Skipped and dropped slots are rows too, each with its reason. `?limit=` takes 1 to 500 (default 50).

A held run has no session, so the item carries the chore, never a thread. `routine.needs` on the event stream carries the same items per chore whenever they change, empty once the chore no longer needs you. post.summary: Fire a `webhook` chore. The node serves this on loopback only, and the caller proves itself with the chore's own token (`authorization: Bearer <token>` from `POST .../hook`), never the node's. The body is untrusted data: it is saved as a file beside the run journal and the run's prompt names that file, never its text. A body over the chore's `maxBytes` (at most 1 MiB) is refused. The run obeys the same hourly caps, lock and grant-set park as every trigger. Since contract 1.17.

get.summary: Every model server this node knows, per node: servers the node manifests advertise and, for nodes without one, servers found by probing the known ports (11434 Ollama, 9931 llama-server, 8080, 1234, 8000, 30000) and fingerprinted by a native route, never by `/v1/models` alone. Each server carries its kind, fingerprint, source (`advertised` or `probed`) and health (`up | loading | saturated | down`); each model carries `installed`, `loaded`, allocated context, the classes it is eligible for (`strong | loop | decide | vision`) with what the others miss, its license and whether that license needs the keeper's acknowledgement, and its cost basis (`local_estimate` for local servers). A host that keeps license acknowledgements also gives each model `released` (the slate's release date, from which a model younger than 30 days reads as preview) and `acknowledgedAt` (when the keeper acknowledged its license, else null), fills a license the server does not report from the slate, and adds `market`: the cloud providers of the inference registry in the same columns (`kind` is the provider's name, `source: registry`, nothing installed or loaded, cost from the price table or null). A market row's health is `down` when the provider is disabled, has no credential, or refused its credential (401 or 403) on its latest turn, `up` once a turn it served answered, and `unverified` until then: listing a provider is not reaching it. A host with a default model also adds `inherits`: per class (`strong`, `loop`, `decide`, `vision`), what a creature or session whose policy says `inherit` gets, as `{ provider, model }` when the host's default model can serve the class, else `{ refused, detail }` with the IR-18 failure code (`missing-capability` for a default the class cannot use, `unconfigured` when the host has none). The class requirements of a local model are measurements of its mill; a cloud model is judged by what keywork.json or its provider's catalogue declares (context length, input modalities, tool calls), anything undeclared is unknown and never a shortfall, and decode speed is never asked of it, so a configured cloud default resolves unless a declared fact falls short; `detail` then names the model and the measurement. `decide` on a model with no decision endpoint or logprobs answers `{ provider, model, decider: builtin, detail }`: the built-in decider asks that model each question, and `detail` says so (since contract 1.20). `?node=` narrows to one node and leaves the market and the inherits out.

200.description: `{ generatedAt, nodes: [{ node, servers: [{ kind, root, port, source, auth, fingerprint, version, health, models }] }], market?, inherits?: { strong, loop, decide, vision } }`.

A server that answers only `/v1/models` comes back `unrecognized` with its listed ids and no capability marked.

Until a license that needs acknowledgement is acknowledged, the model policy resolver refuses that model for every class with the IR-18 code `missing-capability` and the capability `license-acknowledgement`.

get.summary: Every creature's workshop on this node, oldest first: `{ workshops }`, each `{ id, creature, substrate, state, workdir, brokers, limitations, display, createdAt }`. A creature holds at most one workshop and two creatures never share one. `substrate` is `sbx` (a sealed microVM) or `host` (the bare node, whose `workdir` is the workspace that raised it); `limitations` says plainly what a workshop lacks, so a bare host is never shown as sealed. `brokers` names the model-provider credentials the node swaps in on egress; the workshop itself only ever holds sentinels. `display` is true when the substrate can carry a viewable display.

post.summary: Raise a workshop for a creature. `substrate` picks `sbx` or `host`; `egress` lists the only hosts the creature may reach (bare DNS names; `methods` defaults to GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, `any` opens every method, and `port` opens plain TCP such as SSH), everything else stays denied; `brokers` grants model-provider credentials the node holds; `disks` are sized now because an `sbx` disk cannot grow later; `setup` runs once inside after the first start. A `host` workshop works in the workspace this node serves the request from: its `workdir` and jail are the workspace path, and its home under the node's state dir keeps only the workshop's own state; a sealed one never mounts the workspace. An `sbx` workshop is refused before anything is created when an inherited host-wide allow rule would cover a host the creature wants, and is removed again if its egress cannot be applied. `workshop.changed` fires with `change: "created"`.

get.summary: What this node can raise a workshop on: `{ substrates, preferred }`, one row per kind (`sbx`, `compose`, `host`) `{ kind, supported, version, reason, limitations }`. `supported` is asked of the substrate itself (the `sbx` CLI is run for its version and must be the qualified one); an unsupported row's `reason` says why in words the keeper can act on, such as the sbx CLI not being installed. `limitations` names what every workshop of that kind lacks, so a bare host is never offered as sealed. `preferred` is the first supported kind in the order sbx, compose, host, or `null` when none is.

One workshop as `GET /workshops` lists it, plus what the workshop pane shows: `workspace` (how it reaches the keeper's workspace: `access` `direct` for a bare host, which works in the workspace itself with the workspace path as its jail, `working-copy` for a sealed substrate, which never mounts it and works on a copy, or `none` for a bare host raised outside a workspace; `path`, the workspace or `null`; and `returns`, how its work comes back, in words), `egress` (`policy` `deny-all` and `enforced` for a microVM, `none` for a bare host; the creature's own `rules`; the `brokerHosts` its brokered credentials reach), `resources` (the `cpus` and `memory` recorded at creation, the `disks` sized then or `null` for a bare host, and `measured` disk and memory in bytes, each `null` with the reason in `unmeasured` when it cannot be read, such as a stopped microVM), `refusals` (`entries`, the newest fifty things the node refused for this workshop, each `{ at, operation, refused, error }`, and `unreported`, which refusals the node cannot see: an sbx network log has no documented reader yet) and `terminal` (`allowed` and `reason` for typed commands under the keeper's grants, and `log`, the newest fifty typed commands as tool calls `{ at, tool: "bash", origin: "keeper", input, outcome }`).
